title: How much more is one final total than another?
description: Three round marks are chosen that add up to a given final total, and the difference of two final totals is found by taking one bracket from another. The result is checked with p as four and q as one. Keeko's doubt is that the bracket opens to minus twenty one p minus nine q.
teaching_notes: One idea: to find how much more, take one expression from the other, and the minus before the bracket changes every sign inside it. Watch for students who change the first sign inside the bracket and leave the second.

source: {{NAME_3}}'s final score is 23p − 7q. Give three round scores
video_script.why: A learner sees how to find how much more one expression is than another.
video_script.substitution: the book's two final totals, twenty three p minus seven q and twenty one p minus nine q, checked with p as four and q as one
video_script.anchor: the two final totals of the book, twenty three p minus seven q and twenty one p minus nine q
video_script.wrong_answer: the bracket opens to minus twenty one p minus nine q
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko changes the sign of the first term inside the bracket and leaves the second as it is. The minus takes away both terms, so the idea is broken with p as four and q as one.
video_script.payoff_line: {{NAME_3}} has two p plus two q more marks. That is ten when p is four and q is one

final_answer.value: {{NAME_3}} scored 2p + 2q more, which is 10 when p = 4 and q = 1
final_answer.spoken: {{NAME_3}} has two p plus two q more, which is ten when p is four and q is one

names.{{NAME_3}}: Charu's friend, who plays the same quiz with a total of twenty three p minus seven q
names.{{NAME_1}}: plays a quiz in three rounds with a total of twenty one p minus nine q

maths_rules: check with p = 4, q = 1: 2 x 4 + 2 x 1 = 10
Keeko test with p = 4, q = 1: -21p - 9q gives 23 x 4 - 7 x 1 - 21 x 4 - 9 x 1 = 85 - 93 = -8, which is not 10
video_script.design: The two final totals stay on the board; three rounds are chosen for the first, then the second total is taken from the first with its bracket opened and the like terms grouped.
open_questions: The book asks for any three rounds that add up to the total; one possible set is shown, and others are as good.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; {{NAME_3}}'s total 23p − 7q beside {{NAME_1}}'s total 21p − 9q

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the two totals are written side by side
marks.split: three empty round boxes appear under the first total
marks.ask: a question mark appears between the two totals

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is the last part of the quiz question in your book.
<bookmark mark='split'/>{{NAME_3}} has twenty three p minus seven q, and {{NAME_1}} has twenty one p minus nine q.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book wants three rounds that add up to the first total, and how much more it is. What will the difference look like?

beats.on_screen: the two totals stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the two totals

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.two: the numbers 23 and 21 are drawn as two bars
marks.gap: the extra part of the longer bar is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>To find how much more one total is, take the smaller one away from the larger one.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The answer is called the difference.
<bookmark mark='write'/>Twenty three take away twenty one leaves two.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two final totals, with p as four and q as one.

beats.on_screen: To find: three rounds that add to 23p − 7q, and how much more it is than 21p − 9q

marks.find: the words three rounds are written
marks.then: the words how much more are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three rounds that add up to the first total.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then we find how much more it is than the second total.

marks.pick: the three rounds are written in the boxes
marks.add: the p terms and the q terms are grouped and added
marks.total: 23p − 7q is written and matched to the first total

narration: <bookmark mark='pick'/>Step one, try three rounds. They are eight p minus two q, seven p minus three q, and eight p minus two q.
<bookmark mark='add'/>The p terms add to eight plus seven plus eight. The q terms add to two plus three plus two.
<bookmark mark='total'/>That gives twenty three p minus seven q, as the book needs.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, difference = 23p − 7q − (21p − 9q); open the bracket and change both signs: 23p − 7q − 21p + 9q

marks.open: the bracket opens and both of its signs flip

narration: <bookmark mark='diff'/>Step two, the difference is the first total minus the bracket of the second total.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Open the bracket, because the minus takes away both terms, and both signs change.
<bookmark mark='line'/>That gives twenty three p minus seven q minus twenty one p plus nine q.

marks.group: the p terms and the q terms are grouped in two colours

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step three, group the like terms.
<bookmark mark='bracket'/>Twenty three minus twenty one is two, and minus seven plus nine is two.
<bookmark mark='short'/>The difference is two p plus two q. Both p and q are positive, so it is positive.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check with p = 4, q = 1: 85 − 75 = 10 and 2 × 4 + 2 × 1 = 10
narration: <bookmark mark='totals'/>Step four, put p as four and q as one. The first total is eighty five and the second total is seventy five.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>Eighty five minus seventy five is ten.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Two times four plus two times one is also ten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: {{NAME_3}} scored 2p + 2q more, which is 10 when p = 4 and q = 1
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_3}} has two p plus two q more marks. That is ten when p is four and q is one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two totals
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the bracket opens to −21p − 9q, struck out; the test p = 4, q = 1 gives 10 and −8

marks.gap: 10 and −8 appear side by side and do not match
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 2p + 2q stays

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the bracket opens to minus twenty one p minus nine q. Keeko changed only the first sign.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try p as four and q as one.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>That idea gives eighty five minus ninety three, which is minus eight, but the difference is ten.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The minus takes away both terms, so the nine q becomes plus nine q.
